Foundation

3 papers
The discrete state space of the Bost–Connes system naturally describes the physical world.
Dynamics of the Bost–Connes State Space

Dynamics of the Bost–Connes State Space

Shao-Wu HuFirst published 22 September 2026Version 2Open access

We investigate whether the dynamics of the formation, motion, decay, and thermalization of matter in the physical world can be described within a unified and internally consistent mathematical framework. To this end, we start from the local decomposition of the Bost–Connes system and perform a finite p-adic reduction to construct the corresponding state space. Within this space, we characterize stable states relative to a background and establish a complete cycle consisting of free evolution, formation exchange, and pattern reconstruction. Excitation formation, motion, and decay, together with relaxation of the ensemble occupation distribution, are determined by the same joint evolution and its iterations, with the final state of each cycle serving as the initial state of the next. References, observation, and records are incorporated into the same joint construction, giving the evolution of a subject and its observable manifestations a common mathematical basis. Under the corresponding conditions, we derive event statistics, convergence to stationarity, and thermalization, and use joint conservation and entropy balances to relate reversible joint evolution to irreversible system relaxation.

Cosmologyand the Bost–Connes System

Cosmology and the Bost–Connes System

Shao-Wu HuFirst published 15 April 2026October 2026 editionOpen access

Starting from the Bost–Connes parent structure and its finite reductions, we develop a common description of the universe as a whole, its dynamical evolution, and observation from within. Joint coherence and correlations connect different observational channels into one whole, while matter and background change one another through formation, maintenance, and exchange. We construct a joint cycle that retains source memory and compensates energy changes, connecting heat exchange, resource restoration, and matter maintenance, and derive an effective temperature law for collective cooling. The phases of loaded matter provide time references, and correlated light signals connect distant events. Under a common calibration, the ratio of the matter clock rate to the light propagation rate determines the cosmological scale. Explicit dynamics yields finite scale growth, spectral redshift, and residual energy in a dark thermal subspace, showing how energy transfer, the persistence of coherence, and continued resource supply affect thermal evolution and spacetime readings. We further construct formation, unfolding, and complete return under one fixed generator: the endpoint restores a generation-ready preparation, from which regeneration follows.

The Unification of Dynamics

The Unification of Formation, Motion, Decay, and Thermalization of Matter from the Bost–Connes System

Shao-Wu HuFirst published 11 September 2026Version 1Open access

The formation, motion, decay, and thermalization of matter have each been established on the state space of the Bost–Connes system, but the complete cycle map has not yet been constructed. On the finite joint space taking part in the exchange, this paper composes free evolution, formation exchange, and pattern reconstruction into a unitary cycle, with the exchange matrix elements and the environment preparation given as conditions of the construction. A standing wave exchanges continuously with the environment during its propagation, and the system state at the end of the cycle and the outgoing records are determined by the same joint evolution; the environment is refreshed cycle by cycle, and the system continues to evolve under the same map. Retrieval, transit, and transport together determine the maintenance of the standing wave, the change of identity, and the formation of records, while the reverse exchange replenishes formation under the corresponding incident occupation. Record weights are determined, under explicit statistical conditions, by the squared norms of the components of the joint state, and energy and the corresponding conserved charges are balanced between system and environment. Under a specified coherent detection preparation, a conserving cycle realizes position records with controlled error and gives error bounds for the interference visibility; the corresponding finite model gives conditional thermalization during identity maintenance and the equilibrium of formation and exit. Under fixed supply and convergence conditions, the steady total occupation of a linear ensemble equals the product of the production rate and the mean waiting time to the first exit. The evolution of a single standing wave, the occupation of many standing waves, and the statistics of actual records are thereby connected within the same cycle.

Computation

1 paper
The framework as a computing paradigm.
BC State-Space Computer

BC State-Space Computer

Shao-Wu HuFirst published 31 July 2026Version 33Open access

That excitations are countable, that energy is additive, and that independent composition multiplies are three laboratory-level basic facts; their minimal algebraic form is the Bost–Connes (BC) covariance structure. Starting from this we define the BC state-space computer: a controllable physical system that carries the BC covariance relations in finite truncation within finite experimental boundaries. A run is the complete chain that takes external conditions through boundary formation, preparation, constrained evolution, stopping and readout, to return coupling; computation is defined on the run law by a task, a reusable boundary program, physical compilation, and completion criteria. Three structural dilemmas of the prevailing paradigm close at the physical-structure level of this machine. Content processing is carried directly by the state space, and step-by-step replay does not arise; statistics and thermalization are native resources, and pseudorandom reconstruction does not arise; the interface to the world is carried by the physical coupling of transduction and actuation, and symbolic replicas do not arise. The supporting construction consists of the arithmetic workspace (prime occupations carry multiplicative composition, phase sectors carry addition), machine parts organized into an arithmetic and an interaction module, and running instances that progress from elementary operations to sustained tracking. The thermalization mechanism is stated conditionally, all verdict quantities are pre-registered by a numerical twin, and whether devices physically realize them is left to independent experiments.

The Unification of Matter, Forces and Spacetime

The Unification of Matter, Forces, and Spacetime from the Bost–Connes System

Shao-Wu HuFirst published 6 July 2026Version 8Open access

PDF (English)DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23554409
SupplementVideos

Abstract

Starting from a finite p-adic reduction of the Bost–Connes system, we investigate the common dynamical origin of matter, mass, and forces. Matter is characterized as stable excitations whose patterns are preserved under propagation and exchange: the relative phases of their persistent evolution yield mass frequencies, exchange between stable states produces resonance responses, and the influence of the background energy distribution on motion produces a metric response.

We construct the complete process from the formation of a stable pattern to its persistent evolution, bringing path spectral responses, node overlaps, and distributions across generations into a single mass generator. The same mass parameter then governs both the rest-frame energy gap and the inertial response at low momentum, while a common background response provides a unified energy scale.

On the basis of these dynamical relations, we use an odd prime p as a structural parameter to establish evaluation relations for mass spectra and coupling constants. With p=7 and the common energy calibration E0=1 GeV, we obtain an electroweak scale of 246.19 GeV and an inverse electromagnetic coupling of αEM−1=137.03636. The absolute relative deviations of the nine charged-fermion masses from the reference central values are all below 1.5%, and those of the three charged leptons are below 0.003%. The neutrino spectrum predicts absolute masses of 5.07, 9.96, and 50.63 meV for the three mass eigenstates, with a mass-squared difference ratio of Δm312/Δm212=34.52.

About this version

Version 8. This version adds a joint representation of charge, color, spin, and chirality, with a concise explanation in Section 5.2.3 of the main paper and detailed derivations in Supplementary Proofs S15. The new section derives the spin and chirality operators from the stated propagation realization, establishes their compatibility with the internal charge and color representation, treats chirality under the complete mass action, and gives conditional weak chiral selection through a shared contact. The main paper has 192 pages and the separate Supplementary Proofs has 81 pages. The previous formulas and conclusions are retained. Natural selection of the oriented reference and the complete weak vertex remain open; the absolute metric strength retains one physical calibration.

All versions: 10.5281/zenodo.21345360.

Axioms of Quantum Mechanics

Axioms of Quantum Mechanics and the Arithmetic Structure of the Bost–Connes System

Shao-Wu HuFirst published 11 March 2026Version 19Open access

PDF (English)DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21841816

Abstract

The five axioms of von Neumann quantum mechanics are each confirmed by experiment, yet they are not described within a single mathematical framework. Starting from the Bost–Connes system, we perform the p-adic reduction at a prime p and construct the state space H_p = L²(ℤ/p^Kℤ), K = p(p−1)−1, and argue that its structure naturally describes these five axioms. (I) C*-positivity gives the Hilbert space through the GNS construction, (II) invariance under Galois conjugation gives the self-adjoint observables, (III) the CRT decomposition gives the tensor product, and (IV) H = log n generates the unique unitary time evolution. (V) The Born rule comes from the modular structure S = JΔ^{1/2} of the KMS state, its probability weights being the squared moduli of the values of Dirichlet L-functions on the critical line.

The Mechanism of Thermalization

The Mechanism of Thermalization in the Bost–Connes System

Shao-Wu HuFirst published 5 August 2026Version 14Open access

PDF (English)DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21803449

Abstract

Thermalization brings matter toward equilibrium through sustained exchange, while information about the exchange processes remains in the full joint state. Starting from the dynamical cycle established on a finite reduction of the Bost–Connes system, we study the relation between thermal equilibrium, relaxation rates, and local irreversibility. At a fixed finite temperature, with independently refreshed environments, positive exchange shares, and same-temperature restoration as specified here, the full Gibbs state is the unique attracting state of the cycle. The occupation spectrum and coherence factors determine the relaxation rates of different observables and yield a controlled weak-exchange continuous limit on the restored family of states. Energy changes include both thermal exchange and background restoration. This gives conditions for tracking thermal states as the temperature changes, together with the late-time cooling law and its asymptotic corrections for a specified zero-temperature exit process.

The same joint realization determines the environment outputs and entropy balance. The decrease in system relative entropy characterizes the approach to equilibrium, while changes in auxiliary preparations enter the complete correlation and energy balance. The auxiliaries can continue to change even when the system is at equilibrium. We also obtain a return process in which the same interaction acts again on previously used auxiliaries. The endpoint, rate, and time direction of thermalization are thus determined by the equilibrium conditions, actual decay modes, and environmental boundary conditions of one process. They can be tested jointly through occupation, coherence, and energy-flow readings constrained by common parameters.

The Mechanism of the Motion of Matter

The Mechanism of the Motion of Matter from the Bost–Connes System

Shao-Wu HuFirst published 18 August 2026Version 8Open access

PDF (English)DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21992871

Abstract

We investigate how the same matter changes position while undergoing continual maintenance, using the dynamics of a finite Bost–Connes state space. Maintenance preserves the internal structure of matter, while position amplitudes and relative phases evolve under the joint action, with local position currents composing the propagation of the wave packet as a whole. In the uniform propagation model used here, with time calibrated by the total elapsed duration, the internal mass action determines both the rest energy and the curvature of the propagation spectrum. The long-wavelength, low-momentum expansion of a massive branch gives Minc02 = E0, linking the continual maintenance of matter to its inertial response.

The observable manifestations of motion further depend on the records formed during propagation. The double-slit cross term is controlled by the overlap of the complete unread outputs of the two paths; interference in the unconditioned screen distribution disappears when orthogonal records preserve the path distinction. Surviving matter continues to propagate from the conditional state following a record. When a composite object's collective branch is preserved, its conditional position distribution remains concentrated, and spreading and recoil are controlled, the low-speed equation for its center, together with successive records, gives an approximate description of a macroscopic trajectory. The maintenance of matter, coherent quantum propagation, and macroscopic motion are thus connected within the same dynamics.

The Mechanism of Fields

The Mechanism of Fields from the Bost–Connes System

Shao-Wu HuFirst published 27 August 2026Version 5Open access

PDF (English)DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22126955
Dynamical proofs (23 pages)Geometric & optical examples (11 pages)

Abstract

A field is a distribution of background states and correlations formed by the joint evolution of matter and its background. Building on finite joint dynamics in the Bost–Connes state space and established matter identifications, we describe fields through source writing, background transfer, and complete reception. Actual auxiliary returns controlled by edge flux and loop exchange produce electromagnetic storage and, in a controlled long-wavelength window, the Maxwell response. Complete mass endpoints and spatial transport give massive short-range propagation and spin–isospin interaction through pion exchange; color-link loop returns give noncommuting field response. A gravitational background affects both matter maintenance phase and spatial exchange. An explicit occupation preparation with complete package reception gives distinct clock and propagation factors and realizes reciprocal clock–rod scales under finite-time error control. Source, resources, matter, and contact energy remain in one joint evolution. A separate finite construction with directional constraints supplies two accessible positive-frequency radiation modes and reciprocal absorption while retaining the full free spectrum and the unresolved material-readout connection. Each result depends on its stated preparation, spatial deployment, and working window. Relative electromagnetic calibration, persistent strong-background closure, and a common geometric identification of radiation require further dynamical relations.

The Mechanism of Decay

The Mechanism of Decay from the Bost–Connes System

Shao-Wu HuFirst published 4 September 2026Version 3Open access

PDF (English)DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22307012

Abstract

Starting from the dynamics of the Bost–Connes state space and the identification of matter within it, we place maintenance of the original particle, transfer into multiparticle final states, and product propagation within one joint action. The parent and product amplitudes evolve together under this action. Distinguishable records retained by the products then specify the probability balance of uninterrupted survival and first decay. Summing first-decay probabilities over all rounds within each channel gives its branching fraction, while weighting the actual elapsed durations by survival probabilities gives the mean lifetime. In the narrow-resonance regime formed by weak coupling and a smooth outgoing spectrum, the same transfer coupling also gives an energy width, relating mean lifetime to spectral width by T̄cont = ℏ/Γ.

With explicitly specified effective vertices and response matching, product energy sharing, chiral contractions, and barrier propagation yield continuous spectra, helicity suppression, and exponential lifetime hierarchies, respectively. Long lifetime corresponds to suppressed open exits, while stability requires closure of all relevant exit actions. Why the original particle persists, how it transforms, and what spectra and records its products leave thus become related, calculable results within the same dynamical process.
